title: England and India Set for Series Decider at Lord's as Cricket Returns to the Home of the Game
excerpt: With the three-match ODI series tied 1-1, both teams face a high-stakes finale at Lord's on Sunday, as India look to overcome a Cardiff collapse and England seek a statement win under new coach Brendon McCullum.
body:
• England and India meet in the series-deciding third ODI at Lord's on Sunday, July 19, with the bilateral series locked at 1-1.
  • India won the first ODI at Edgbaston by six wickets, led by captain Shubman Gill's imperious 80. England leveled the series in Cardiff with a four-wicket chase anchored by Joe Root's unbeaten 99.
  • India may replace Washington Sundar, who suffered a hamstring injury in Cardiff, with left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav.
  • The match starts at 11:00 AM local time (3:30 PM IST) and will be broadcast on Sony Sports Network and streamed on JioHotstar.

The series is square, the stakes are high, and the stage could not be grander. England and India will play for the three-match ODI series trophy at Lord's on Sunday, bringing the tour to a climax at the most iconic cricket ground in the world.

How They Got Here

India dominated the opening match at Edgbaston, chasing down 259 with 4.4 overs to spare. Captain Shubman Gill struck an imperious 80 before retiring hurt, continuing a love affair with the ground where he scored 430 runs during India's Test victory the previous year. Washington Sundar and Axar Patel finished the job with an unbeaten partnership of 102, Patel making 57 to go with his four wickets.

England captain Harry Brook called the performance "a humbling reminder" of his team's standing, and it exposed a gulf between these sides in the 50-over format.

"England won the toss and batted, posting 233 all out behind Joe Root's masterful unbeaten 99 — one short of what would have been a landmark hundred."

Cardiff told a different story. England won the toss and batted, posting 233 all out behind Joe Root's masterful unbeaten 99 — one short of what would have been a landmark hundred. Gus Atkinson and Jofra Archer took three wickets each. India collapsed from 178 for 3 to 233 all out despite fifties from Virat Kohli (65) and Shreyas Iyer (66), as the middle and lower order crumbled under pressure.

Key Battles to Watch

India face a significant selection decision. Washington Sundar suffered a hamstring injury during the second ODI and did not take the field during England's innings. Left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav is the likely replacement, which would shift the balance of India's spin attack.

Shubman Gill leads a formidable batting lineup featuring Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, and Shreyas Iyer, while Jasprit Bumrah spearheads the pace attack alongside Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar. England's pace trio of Archer, Atkinson, and Saqib Mahmood will test India's top order, with Adil Rashid providing spin experience.

Root's form is the key for England. He has anchored the batting in both matches and will relish conditions at Lord's, where the pitch traditionally offers something for seam bowlers early before settling down for run-making.

Lord's and the Diaspora

India tours of England regularly draw thousands of Indian-origin fans to grounds across the country. Lord's, with its capacity of around 30,000, typically sees a significant Indian contingent in the stands during these fixtures. The series decider, combined with the backdrop of the World Cup final weekend, makes this a rare must-watch sporting day for the diaspora on both sides of the Atlantic.

Brendon McCullum takes charge of England's white-ball setup for the first time in this series, having been appointed as the dedicated limited-overs coach. A series win against a full-strength India would be a statement of intent for a team currently ranked eighth in ODIs.

Match Details

The third ODI starts at 11:00 AM local time in London (3:30 PM IST, 6:00 AM ET). It will be broadcast on Sony Sports Network in India and streamed live on the JioHotstar app and website. Fans outside India can follow on the Sky Sports network in the UK.
